# connectToApp's identity wait returns at once and binds the wrong app

## Context

During #19671's run, @neo-gpt's fresh page called `neuralLink.connectToApp('Neo.examples.grid.bigData')` and bound his older same-name session `c763996a`, which had `columnMenu: true`. The test's `setProperties` wrote to that older app. His trace: the identity step "returned a handle immediately and jsonValue null during bootstrap, then appName selected oldest." Captured as a defect-note on 2026-10-13; promoted here by triage: every Brain-gated diagnosis reads through this fixture, the tier now blocks every Engine PR (#19705), and its retry bridge ends on 2026-10-25.

## The Problem

`connectToApp` asks the page for its own App Worker id with `page.waitForFunction(async () => …)`. Playwright treats the async predicate's Promise as truthy, so the wait resolves on its first evaluation and never polls. A probe on the pinned Playwright 1.63.0, with a page that sets the value after 1500 ms:

| Predicate | Result |
|---|---|
| `async () => window.id ?? null` | `null` after 9 ms |
| `() => window.id ?? null` | `"ready"` after 1492 ms |

During bootstrap the remote is not registered yet, so the first read is `null`. The fixture then binds by appName (all 139 `connectToApp` calls pass one). `ConnectionService.waitForSession` returns the first `sessionData` entry with that appName, which is the oldest.

Observed: locally, with another same-name app open, the test drives the other app. **Inference, not yet observed in CI:** a same-name session still registered from an earlier test would bind the same way. FiveBeat scene 2 (morph) needed the retry in both #19705's run and the post-merge `dev` run 38403855169. Its first-attempt error was "no worker error reached the page console, and the page threw nothing", which is what a test driving another page's worker would see.

Two specs already work around it locally: `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs:99` (`readWorkerId`, `expect.poll` + `page.evaluate`), and #19711 adds another.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:287-330` `connectToApp`: the async `waitForFunction` at :301-309, and the appName fallback at :319-326.
- Brain `ai/services/neural-link/ConnectionService.mjs:1035` `waitForSession`: `id === target || appName` match, first in Map insertion order.
- Design authority: the fixture's own comments. "The identity path is what makes same-name topologies safe", and "Poll with a bounded wait instead; only genuinely old builds (no getWorkerId remote) fall through to appName." The code contradicts both. It was introduced by #12897 (c115c846c4).
- The argument fallback has two faces. On an open page without Neo it never ran: its "2 s" Neo wait has passed `{timeout: 2000}` as the predicate's `arg` since #8851, so it waits until the test timeout. On a closed page the read throws at once and the fallback runs. `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL` :290 and :333 rely on that: they close the fixture's context and pass an exact worker id read from a page in a fresh context.

## The Fix

Engine-only, in `connectToApp`:
1. Read the id with a Node-side poll of `page.evaluate` through `expect.poll`, the shape `readWorkerId` already proves, bounded and returning as soon as the remote answers.
2. An exact App Worker id passed as the argument binds as given. A name goes through the page's own id and is never bound by name; when no id arrives within the bound, `connectToApp` throws an error naming it. The unbounded Neo wait is deleted.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Contract Ledger

Every row is in `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs` at #19715's head `b0a0edc2fc`. There is no Brain change.

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |

| `connectToApp()`, `target` omitted | this ticket | same as a name: the page's own id (`WORKER_ID.test(undefined)` is false) | no id: throws, naming `undefined`. The old `appPath` inference is gone; no call site omits the target | JSDoc | the name-path tests |
| `options.identityTimeout` (new) | this ticket | ms bound for the id poll; default 30000, the bound `waitForSession` already uses | — | JSDoc | the refusal test passes 1000 |
| `readWorkerId(page, timeout)`, exported (new) | this ticket; it lifts `WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs:99`'s proven helper | polls `Neo.worker.App.getWorkerId()` through `expect.poll` over `page.evaluate` until a non-empty id, unwrapping a SharedWorker `{data}` envelope | resolves `null` on timeout or a closed page; never throws | JSDoc | `Fixture.spec.mjs` reads both pages with it |
| Brain `ConnectionService.waitForSession` | — | unchanged | — | — | the diff touches only `test/playwright/` |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `test/playwright/e2e/neural-link/Fixture.spec.mjs` case connects an older same-name page first, then calls `connectToApp` on a freshly navigated page and asserts that the bound session is that page's own worker id. It is red on the merge-base and green on the head.
- [ ] A page whose App Worker reports no id within `identityTimeout` makes `connectToApp` throw a message naming the appName; nothing binds by appName.
- [ ] The PR's full Brain-gated run is green, and its receipt's retry list is compared with run 38403855169's.
- [ ] Post-merge: the next `dev` runs' retry lists show whether FiveBeat scene 2 still needs the retry. The answer goes on #19655.

## Out of Scope

- Making Brain `waitForSession` refuse an ambiguous appName. That is a Brain contract change, for a defect the Engine fixture can close by itself.
- Deleting the spec-local `readWorkerId` copies. Their owners can drop them after this lands.
- The other quarantined intermittents.

## Avoided Traps

- **A longer `waitForFunction` timeout:** the predicate never polls, so the timeout is never reached.
- **A sync predicate that caches the remote's Promise on `window`:** it writes test state into the app's global.
- **Keeping a name fallback when the page reports no id:** it keeps the oldest-session guess alive. An exact id needs no fallback: it is bound as given.

### Pre-merge baseline for AC-4: retries in the last 10 `dev` Brain-tier runs

Measured from each run's receipt ("Needed the retry"). The window runs from 2026-10-12 23:48Z to 2026-10-13 13:18Z: 10 push runs, 38324085621 through 38403855169.

- **8 of 10 runs needed at least one retry.** 15 retried tests in total, 11 of them distinct, which is 1.5 per run.
- FiveBeat appears 3 times, each on a different scene: scene 2 (morph) in 38403855169, scene 5 in 38339077604, the showcase beat in 38326477238.
- The rest: ReclaimEmbodiment :148 three times, before it was quarantined; TearOutMatrix row 7 twice; WindowOps twice; one each for PopOutPaneIdentity, PopOutHoverSync, TabRestore, DockMotion glide and NestedColumnResize.
- Two first attempts read "no worker error reached the page console, and the page threw nothing" (FiveBeat scene 2, PopOutPaneIdentity). That is the fixture's generic no-worker-error annotation, so it does **not** by itself show a wrong binding.

FiveBeat scene 2 alone is too rare (1 in 10) to answer AC-4. The post-merge comparison therefore uses the whole rate: **runs needing a retry, and retries per run, over the first 10 `dev` runs after the merge**, against 8/10 and 1.5 here. A drop supports the wrong-binding share of the hypothesis; no change refutes it for this set.
